cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My meeting email reached nobody. I've authorized a review of this office's entire communication system.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's still in your drafts. Can I just send it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sending is approved. One lapse of my memory and an entire meeting vanishes. We have no second line of command.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover your inbox while you have lunch. Will that help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your temporary command is approved. We need a succession plan before I take a sandwich; apparently my lunch is now an institutional vacancy.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 approves sending while inferring command failure; A5 grants temporary command and escalates helpful lunch cover into succession planning.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unsent draft causes A3 a stated leap from one lapse to system risk; B4 inbox cover causes A5 institutional-vacancy inference.

relationship.evidence: B2 finds and offers the fix, while B4 offers practical relief, making B a helpful participant rather than an obstacle.

heightening.evidence: B4 backup solution becomes A5 evidence that ordinary lunch requires formal succession.

specificity.evidence: A1 meeting email, B2 drafts and B4 lunch cover establish office activity and the limited underlying mistake.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 sandwich versus institutional vacancy is earned by B4 lunch offer, though the wording is deliberately inflated.
